title: The Rider on the White Ridge
summary: After Rowan Hold, Veyra and Samuel catch the trio on the Long Mile and agree to stop operating ahead of them. Jessa allows them to travel on the same road only if they remain in sight. During that uneasy new arrangement, Eva spots a solitary Rider on a pale ridge.

panelPlan.text: Wide Long Mile: Veyra and Samuel have caught up after Rowan Hold. Their bedrolls remain separate from the rig and they walk a few paces apart, making the new arrangement visibly provisional.

Jessa makes the condition plain: no more disappearing ahead to prepare a town. Veyra accepts because observing Kael without contaminating the next encounter now serves her investigation better too. Eva notices a mounted silhouette on the southern ridge while they are still talking.
Kael looks once at the Rider, sees no immediate problem and keeps walking beside the rig. The others gradually shift attention from the travel arrangement to the figure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: No notes left for towns. No helpful strangers. No 'accidental' conversations.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Stay where she can see you and you'll save us all time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: You say that like I'm the dangerous one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I said it like Jessa has rules.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: There's a rider on the south ridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Then let them have their ridge.

directionInline.text: The group composition must be caused, not assumed. Veyra stops the ahead/behind method because it contaminates her own evidence; Jessa tolerates open co-travel because keeping the manipulators visible is safer than letting them vanish ahead. The Rider's first appearance remains completely ordinary.

title: Closing Distance
summary: Eva and Veyra angle toward the ridge to get a better look. After several minutes of walking, the Rider appears no closer despite terrain that should have reduced the distance.

panelPlan.text: Eva and Veyra cross a shallow dry wash while Jessa and Samuel remain with the rig.
A foreground rock and ridge notch provide clear visual landmarks. The Rider remains positioned against the same notch.
Eva checks behind them, surprised by how far they have actually walked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: Enough that I wouldn't be asking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: I hate pretending maybe is no.

directionInline.text: Eva and Veyra are the ones crossing the wash, so only they speak in the close exchange. Keep a credible mirage/terrain explanation available; the strangeness comes from repeated comparison, not one impossible panel.

title: The Longer Route
summary: Jessa takes a route that should intersect the Rider's ridge. The landmarks confirm the group is moving correctly, yet the Rider now appears on a farther ridge beyond the first.

panelPlan.text: The group follows a clear natural cut toward the southern ridge. Kael marks the original ridge with a distinctive split stone.
They crest it and find no tracks, rider or recent disturbance.
Across the next basin, the same unreadable silhouette stands against a farther horizon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Could be two people who own similar hats.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Good. Let's keep it that way.

directionInline.text: Do not confirm identity through impossible detail. They are comparing silhouette and behavior, not seeing a supernatural face.

title: When They Stop
summary: Kael refuses to spend the day chasing a person who has not approached them. The group resumes its original route. Near sunset, the Rider appears on a low rise much closer than before.

panelPlan.text: Kael turns back toward the road while Eva argues for one more ridge. Samuel quietly agrees with Kael.
Hours later the group makes a small evening camp beside the road, the southern ridges now behind them.
Jessa looks up from the fire and sees the Rider standing on a low rise perhaps a few hundred yards away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We finally have something that doesn't make sense.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: It's still a stranger who hasn't asked us for anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You were more useful when you were lying to us.

directionInline.text: The closer reappearance after abandoning pursuit is the first event that should feel genuinely difficult to reconcile with the earlier distance.

title: Veyra Has Seen It
summary: Veyra admits she has seen the same distance behavior before, months earlier, before Samuel began planting identities and before she had confirmed Kael's route.

panelPlan.text: The group watches the Rider from camp without approaching. Veyra is more unsettled than Eva has ever seen her.
Samuel asks whether this is the figure Veyra once refused to explain in her notes.
Veyra says she saw a Rider outside Red Wash while pursuing a completely different lead; riding toward it made it seem farther away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: Months ago. Before Samuel. Before I knew Kael's route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: Until my horse was lathered and the rider was farther away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Then maybe it isn't following me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: I didn't say it was following you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: No. You just looked at me.

directionInline.text: This is a causal complication, not an answer. The Rider may not originate from Kael's presence at all.

title: Nearer in the Morning
summary: Nobody pursues the Rider overnight. At first light the figure is gone from the rise, but a fresh silhouette stands on the road behind them, closer than anyone can explain without invoking a second rider or impossible movement.

panelPlan.text: Pre-dawn camp: no one is sleeping well, though Kael is making coffee rather than mounting a watchful pose.
The rise is empty at sunrise. Eva visibly relaxes for one second.
Jessa turns toward the road they traveled yesterday. The Rider stands there in the distance, close enough to be unmistakably present but still too far for facial detail.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: Do you want a bad one?

directionInline.text: This is the first genuinely uncanny threshold. Keep the Rider distant and unreadable; impossibility lives in spatial behavior, not spectacle.
